{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. The distribution shows right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81), so log-transform or robust ANOVA (Welch's) should be considered. Given unequal group sizes (n ranges 3,323 to 48,846), Welch's ANOVA is preferred to handle heteroscedasticity.",
    "For Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean 0.73, making standard ANOVA inappropriate. Use binomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or equivalently a chi-squared test of independence. Report odds ratios relative to Sham baseline.",
    "For Path Efficiency: Continuous but bounded [0, ~30] with mean 0.47 and heavy right tail (max=29.8). Standard ANOVA assumptions likely violated. Consider log-transform, rank-based ANOVA (Kruskal-Wallis), or generalized linear model with appropriate family (Gamma).",
    "For Average Speed: Continuous, approximately normal by central limit theorem given large N, but check for outliers (max=75.35). One-way ANOVA acceptable with outlier-robust checks or Welch's ANOVA due to unequal n.",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): Bounded [0,1], right-skewed (mean=0.38, max=1.0). Beta regression or arcsine-square-root transform with ANOVA, or non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis as conservative alternative."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed via experimental design; verify no temporal autocorrelation within mice by checking if trials are randomized or blocked appropriately.",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for each paradigm group; given N>3000 per group for most paradigms, central limit theorem supports mean comparisons but not variance-based inference.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test critical given 15:1 ratio in group sizes (Combined n=48,846 vs Bright Visual Only n=3,323). Welch's ANOVA or heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors required.",
    "Outliers: Examine boxplots for Time-to-Target (max=201s) and Path Efficiency (max=29.8); winsorize or use robust methods if outliers are data errors.",
    "For Success (binary): Check for complete separation—Sham has 27% success vs 67-78% for active conditions, so no separation issues expected."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus test significant for continuous variables: Games-Howell post-hoc tests (unequal variances, unequal n) or Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction for non-parametric analyses.",
    "Specific contrasts of interest: Combined vs ICMS Only (additive vs single modality), Combined vs Bright Visual Only (multiplicative vs visual alone), Sham vs each active condition (effect presence), Dim vs Bright Visual Only (intensity effect).",
    "For Success (logistic regression): Estimated marginal means with pairwise comparisons using z-tests, multiplicity-adjusted p-values (Tukey or Bonferroni).",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d for continuous variables (pooled SD), odds ratios for Success, with 95% confidence intervals."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance: longest Time-to-Target (4.68s vs 2.56-3.14s), lowest Success (27.3% vs 67-78%), lowest Path Efficiency (0.31 vs 0.43-0.50), lowest Average Speed (10.74 vs 11.97-12.83), and lowest AD (0.24 vs 0.34-0.40).",
    "Combined expected to show best or near-best performance: fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s), highest Success (78.0%), highest Average Speed (12.83), highest AD (0.40), with Path Efficiency comparable to Bright Visual Only (0.50 vs 0.50).",
    "Visual-only paradigms: Bright Visual Only expected to outperform Dim Visual Only on Success (78.5% vs 67.3%), Time-to-Target (2.61s vs 3.14s), Path Efficiency (0.50 vs 0.43), and AD (0.39 vs 0.34), with similar Average Speed (12.68 vs 11.97).",
    "ICMS Only intermediate: Performance between Combined and Dim Visual Only on most metrics, suggesting visual stimulation provides additional benefit beyond intracortical microstimulation alone.",
    "AD pattern suggests Sham produces most directed/straight paths (lowest angular dispersion), while active stimulation increases exploratory/curved trajectories, with Combined showing highest angular dispersion."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in group sizes (Combined n=48,846 vs Bright Visual Only n=3,323) reduces power for comparisons involving smaller groups and requires Welch's or robust methods.",
    "No mouse-level random effects specified; if multiple trials per mouse, repeated-measures structure ignored leading to inflated Type I error. Mixed-effects models recommended.",
    "Success is binary—standard ANOVA inappropriate, requiring logistic regression or non-parametric alternatives.",
    "Path Efficiency and AD bounded distributions violate ANOVA normality assumptions; transformations or specialized models needed.",
    "No covariates (e.g., trial number, learning effects, mouse identity) included in planned analysis, potentially confounding paradigm effects.",
    "Cross-sectional analysis of summary data precludes examination of trial-by-trial dynamics or within-mouse variability."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMM) for continuous outcomes and generalized linear mixed models (GLMM, binomial) for Success, with Stim Paradigm as fixed effect and Mouse as random intercept, including random slope for trial order if learning effects suspected. For bounded outcomes (Path Efficiency, AD), consider beta regression with mixed effects or robust quantile regression. Report estimated marginal means with multiplicity-adjusted confidence intervals rather than raw ANOVA."
}
